search_objective: Identify authoritative sources reporting Dengue cases, deaths, hospitalizations, and subnational breakdowns for Brazil during Q1 2024 (2024-01-01 to 2024-03-31), covering official Brazilian public health agencies, international organizations, structured surveillance databases, and news/situation reports.
search_reasoning: Brazil's primary dengue surveillance authority is the Ministério da Saúde (Ministry of Health) and its Secretaria de Vigilância em Saúde (SVS), which publishes weekly epidemiological bulletins ("Boletim Epidemiológico") and InfoDengue/SINAN data. Q1 2024 was a historically severe dengue season in Brazil, so official bulletins, PAHO/WHO situation reports, and major news outlets are all likely to carry quantitative data. Portuguese-language queries targeting Brazilian official terminology ("casos", "óbitos", "boletim epidemiológico", "situação epidemiológica") are essential alongside English queries, because the primary authoritative sources publish in Portuguese. The upstream plan covers English-language queries well but lacks Portuguese-language official-agency and international-org queries with Brazilian agency-specific terminology. Given the 4-query-per-iteration cap, this iteration prioritises: (1) Portuguese-language Brazilian MoH/SVS official bulletin query — highest yield for all target fields; (2) PAHO situation report query in English — strong international validation source; (3) Portuguese-language news/media query targeting the outbreak peak period — supports subnational location and date granularity; (4) English-language WHO/PAHO/ProMED structured query — cross-validation. Upstream queries q_exec_001–q_exec_010 are retained for iteration 2 if needed, but their exact phrasing (quoted exact-match strings with date ranges embedded) may suppress relevant results; refined open queries are preferred here.

query_batch.query: dengue Brasil 2024 boletim epidemiológico casos óbitos Ministério da Saúde SVS janeiro fevereiro março
query_batch.query_rationale: Portuguese is the primary language of Brazilian official health publications. Targeting MoH/SVS bulletin terminology ('boletim epidemiológico', 'casos', 'óbitos') with month names for Q1 2024 maximises retrieval of the highest-authority source for all target fields including subnational breakdowns.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: Brazilian Ministry of Health (Ministério da Saúde) or SVS weekly epidemiological bulletin (Boletim Epidemiológico) with national and state-level dengue case and death counts for Q1 2024
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: gov.br domain, SVS authorship, official bulletin numbering, SINAN/InfoDengue data citation

query_batch.query_rationale: PAHO is the primary international body monitoring dengue in the Americas and regularly publishes situation reports with Brazil-specific data. This provides cross-validation of Brazilian MoH figures and may include hospitalization and case-classification breakdowns.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: PAHO (Pan American Health Organization) or WHO epidemiological alert, situation report, or regional dengue update covering Brazil Q1 2024 with cumulative case and death counts
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: paho.int or who.int domain, official situation report or epidemiological alert document, dated 2024

query_batch.query_rationale: Portuguese-language news sources frequently report subnational (state and municipality) dengue data citing official secretariats, filling gaps in locality and date_reported fields not always visible in national bulletins. The 2024 Q1 dengue season was widely covered in Brazilian media.
query_batch.expected_source_type_or_evidence: Brazilian news outlets (e.g., G1/Globo, Agência Brasil, Folha de S.Paulo, UOL) reporting on the 2024 dengue outbreak with state-level or city-level case and death figures, citing official sources
query_batch.expected_trust_signal: Named Brazilian news outlet, quotes from Ministério da Saúde or state health secretariats, specific numeric figures with dates

query_batch.expected_trust_signal: ProMED post with archive number, ECDC rapid risk assessment document, HealthMap event ID, dated within Q1 2024

language_or_localization_reasoning: Portuguese is the official language of Brazil and all primary surveillance outputs from the Ministério da Saúde, SVS, and state health secretariats are published in Portuguese. Key Brazilian epidemiological terms include: 'dengue' (same), 'casos confirmados/prováveis/suspeitos' (confirmed/probable/suspected cases), 'óbitos' (deaths), 'internações/hospitalizações' (hospitalizations), 'boletim epidemiológico' (epidemiological bulletin), 'semana epidemiológica' (epidemiological week), 'situação epidemiológica' (epidemiological situation), 'Ministério da Saúde' (Ministry of Health), 'Secretaria de Vigilância em Saúde' (SVS), 'SINAN' (national disease notification system), 'InfoDengue' (dengue surveillance platform). Queries q1_001 and q1_003 are in Portuguese to maximise retrieval from Brazilian official and media sources. Queries q1_002 and q1_004 are in English targeting international organisations and global surveillance databases that publish in English.
trust_considerations: Prefer gov.br official domains for Brazilian MoH/SVS sources over secondary aggregators
PAHO and WHO documents carry high international authority for cross-validation
News sources are acceptable for subnational/locality data only when they explicitly cite official health secretariat figures
ProMED posts are acceptable as structured secondary sources that link to primary official reports
Avoid sources that do not cite a primary official data source for numeric figures
Portuguese-language sources from Brazilian official agencies take precedence over English translations for accuracy of case definitions and counts
stop_condition_hypothesis: Stop after this iteration if results yield at least one Brazilian MoH/SVS bulletin with national case/death counts, at least one PAHO or WHO situation report, and at least one subnational breakdown. Proceed to iteration 2 if subnational (state-level) data, hospitalization counts, or case-classification breakdowns (confirmed/probable/suspected) remain uncovered.

search_reasoning: Iteration 1 returned strong broad coverage of the 2024 Brazil dengue season but the top results are predominantly full-year 2024 or post-Q1 snapshots (e.g., October 2024, December 2024, full-year totals). The single confirmed Q1-specific result (gov.br Boletim Epidemiológico vol.55 no.11, referencing SE4/2024 with ~260k probable cases) is promising but covers only one early bulletin. Critical gaps remain: (1) no Q1-specific (Jan–Mar 2024) national cumulative case/death/hospitalization snapshot with confirmed+probable+suspected breakdown; (2) no PAHO situation report dated within Q1 2024 (the PAHO results found are from October 2024); (3) no state-level (subnational) Q1 2024 data beyond a partial Minas Gerais snippet with unclear dates; (4) no hospitalization counts for Q1 2024; (5) no ProMED/ECDC Q1-specific posts confirmed. The Minas Gerais state bulletin (saude.mg.gov.br) and InfoDengue platform appeared but without Q1-specific evidence quotes. Iteration 2 must target: (a) additional Brazilian MoH bulletins specifically covering SE1–SE13 (weeks 1–13 of 2024, i.e., Jan–Mar); (b) PAHO epidemiological alerts or situation reports published in Q1 2024 (Jan–Mar); (c) high-burden state secretariat bulletins (São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, Goiás, Distrito Federal) for subnational Q1 data; (d) hospitalization data from Brazilian MoH or state sources. This is the final permitted iteration (max_iterations=2), so queries must be maximally targeted.
